To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

an epitaxial vertical MOSFET incorporating an epitaxially grown junction stop structure delivers improved short channel effects and drive current performance compared with a VMOST with a bulk channel.
a VMOST with a retrograde epitaxial channel in a stacked siliconinsulator structure delivers improved drive current and short channel characteristics compared with a conventional device.
the VMOST with an epitaxial retrograde channel and junction stop delivers improved short channel effects, higher drive current, and higher current gain compared with conventional MOSFETs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fabrication of vertical MOSFETs with a stacked silicon-insulating structure and the use of a retrograde channel.
the development of the VMOST structure for future high-performance logic and memory applications.
improving the performance of vertical MOSFETs in a 65 nm CMOS technology node.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the epitaxial channel VMOST is a very attractive device for high performance applications.
the VMOST structure is a viable candidate for future scaled MOSFET devices.
the VMOST with an epitaxial layer and a junction stop is a very promising candidate for high-speed and low-power logic applications in the sub-50 nm regime.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the epitaxial channel structure combined with the junction stop is an effective way of improving VMOST performance in the sub- 100 nm regime.
a VMOST structure incorporating an epitaxially grown channel and a junction stop can deliver high drive current and improved short channel effects.
this device structure can provide a high drive current and good short channel control simultaneously.
The main takeaway from our work is that
VMOSTs with epitaxial channels and junction stops are promising for future high performance vertical transistors.
a combination of a shallow junction and an epitaxial retrograde channel in a VMOST structure can deliver improved short channel performance and drive current.

a VMOST with a stacked silicon-insulater structure and an epitaxial retrograde channel is a promising candidate to achieve high-performance and low-power operation for the next generation of 3-D integrated circuits.
